description: A lattice pavilion structure evaluated through shell analysis, catenary form-finding and beam optimization for 3D-printable fabrication.
body: Tunnel Pavilion investigates the design and structural evaluation of a lattice shell using computational geometry. The surface originates from a parametric equation — adjusting scale, pinch strength and wave amplitude — then reshaped with catenary curves; a shell analysis in Karamba3D compares the original mesh against the catenary-reshaped one, trading a small increase in deflection for lower von Mises stress.

The shell is then converted into a lattice system and tested under self-weight and wind loads with recycled reinforced-glass beam elements. Among the lattice topologies generated with the Crystallon plug-in, StarTet and BC Cubic lattices gave the best balance of structural performance and fabrication efficiency — the optimized lattice reached a total beam length of 3,262 m with a maximum deflection of 12.5 mm and a utilization ratio of just 0.29%, leaving room for further thickness optimization.
